questions.question_text: Why is an extrapolated prediction generally less reliable than an interpolated one?

options.text: Because there is no evidence that the relationship continues unchanged beyond the recorded data.
Because extending a line of best fit automatically changes its gradient.
options.why: Extending a line doesn't change its gradient — the concern is whether the trend continues, not the slope.

options.text: Because a line of best fit can only be trusted at the exact points that were plotted.
options.why: This overstates the limitation — interpolation between recorded points is generally reliable.

options.text: Because extrapolated predictions always require more complicated arithmetic.
options.why: The reliability issue is about the data's range, not the difficulty of the calculation.

questions.solution_text:
Interpolation is supported by recorded data on both sides, so the fitted line is well tested there.
Extrapolation predicts beyond the recorded data, where there is no evidence the same relationship continues, so it is less reliable.
